item.title: Takachiho Shrine — Guide
item.description: Takachiho Shrine (Takachiho Jinja), founded some 1,900 years ago, is the spiritual heart of the mythologically rich town of Takachiho in northern Miyazaki. Set in a serene, atmospheric grove of towering ancient cedar trees, the weathered wooden shrine radiates a deep sense of age and sanctity. Among its treasures is a magnificent pair of 800-year-old ‘meoto sugi’ (husband-and-wife cedar trees), joined at the roots, around which couples walk hand in hand for blessings of love, marriage and harmony.

item.title: Takachiho Yokagura Night Dance — Guide
item.description: Takachiho yokagura is an ancient sacred dance (kagura) dedicated to the gods, and one of the most captivating cultural experiences in Miyazaki. Rooted in the town’s deep connection to Japanese creation mythology, the dances retell the famous legend of the sun goddess Amaterasu, who hid in a cave and plunged the world into darkness until the other gods lured her out with music and dance. In the traditional season (mid-November to early February), villages across Takachiho perform the full ritual — all 33 dances over an entire night, in farmhouses warmed by fires, a profound community tradition recognised by UNESCO.
